title: Detection of endogenous and drug-modulated CYP3A activity in cells using LC-MS/MS﻿
protocol: Prepare a source plate containing DMSO, ketoconazole, and test compound(s) of interest.
Dispense 100 nL from the source plate to the assay plate containing cells.
Obtain cells at a concentration of 333,333 cells/mL.
Calculate total volume required for dispensing 30 µL/well per well.
Plate cells using Thermo Fisher multidrop combi with small bore tubing.
Add doxycycline to inducible cell lines if applicable.
Incubate cells at 37°C for 24 hours to allow for attachment.
Briefly centrifuge compound source plate and assay plate.
Dispense 100 nL from the compound plate into appropriate wells of the assay plate according to template.
Add 100nL from a 1.5 mM stock of midazolam into all wells of the assay plate (to yield a final concentration of 5 µM).
Return cells to incubator for 24 hours.

Make a standard plate of midazolam and 1-hydroxymidazolam (1OH-MDZ) to be used as calibration standards for the quantitative analysis. Standards should be prepared in the same media which cells are cultured in and using a same final DMSO concentration as the assay plate.
Remove assay plate from incubator and briefly centrifuge along with standard plate.
Quench the reactions by adding 60 μL of acetonitrile containing 4 μg/mL Warfarin to the assay and standard plates.
Seal the assay and standard plates.
Centrifuge the sealed plates at 4,000 RPM for 20 minutes.
Prepare corresponding mass spec appropriate plates (typically v-bottom or round-bottom plates).
Label the plates with corresponding names (“Standard”, “Plate 1”, “Plate 2”, etc.).
Add 30 μL of Milli Q H₂O to all wells in the empty mass spec plates.
Briefly centrifuge the mass spec plates.
Transfer 30 μL of the supernatant from assay plates into the 30 μL of Milli Q H₂O in the mass spec plates.
Seal the resulting mass spec plates.
Thaw plates (if applicable) and centrifuge briefly.
Inject 10 μL of each unknown sample into a UPLC HSS C18 column.
Inject 10 μL of each calibration sample into a UPLC HSS C18 column.
Prepare solvent A with 0.1% formic acid in water.
Prepare solvent B with 0.1% formic acid in acetonitrile.
Use a Valco Valve to desalt the eluant to waste for the first 0.5 minutes.
Perform chromatographic separation by gradient elution at a constant flow rate of 1 mL min^-1 for 2 minutes.
Start gradient elution: At 0.0 min, use 90% A–10% B.
At 0.3 min, change to 80% A–20% B and maintain until 1.35 min.
From 1.65 min to 1.95 min, change to 5% A–95% B then to 10% A–95% B.
At 2.00 min, revert to 90% A-10% B.
Direct the remaining eluates to the triple quadrupole mass spectrometer.
Perform LC-MS/MS using positive polarity at 3000V.
Set the source temperature at 650°C.
Configure gas settings for nitrogen: Gas 1 and Gas 2 at 60, curtain gas at 20, collision gas at 10.
Monitor reactions with m/z transitions of 326 to 291 for midazolam, 342 to 324 for 1OH-MDZ, and 309 to 163 for Warfarin as internal standard.
Set declustering potentials at 120 V for MDZ, 70 V for 1-OH MDZ, and 57 V for the internal standard.
Set entrance potentials at 12 V for MDZ, 12 V for 1-OH MDZ, and 12 V for the internal standard.
Configure collision energy settings: 35V for MDZ, 30V for 1-OH MDZ, and 44V for the internal standard.
Set collision cell exit potential at 27 V for MDZ, 40 V for 1-OH MDZ, and 20 V for the internal standard.
Acquire data with Analyst 1.6.3 software.
Process data using MultiQuant 2.1.1 or similar software.
Load LC-MS/MS results into a spreadsheet.
Format results in units of nM for abundance of 1OH-MDZ for each compound and cell line tested.
Create an XY data table using GraphPad Prism software.
Transform compound concentrations to a Log10 scale.
Normalize the data by setting Y = 0 for defining 0% and taking the average of the DMSO column for defining 100%.
Fit the data with a curve using nonlinear regression and select the equation ‘log(inhibitor) vs. response – Variable slope (four parameters)’.
Find the IC50 values for each compound by clicking on the ‘Nonlin fit’ table of results.
